name: mycrew
description: A four-layer harness for Claude Code, each layer driving the one below: primitives and house rules, a pipeline that carries a task from decision to hardened code, a product plane holding what the product must do together with a board holding what is being done about it right now, and the crew that builds it — a chief over the whole product, a lead to a feature, a worker to an assignment. Install mycrew-tools first.

plugins.name: mycrew-tools
plugins.description: Layer 1/4 — the primitives. Small, project-agnostic skills you reach for mid-work: /slap resets a fix that has stopped working, /likec4 draws architecture as code, /reminder pins a rule as a hard constraint, /retract hunts down information declared wrong and cuts it out. Ships the house rule files too. Everything above builds on this.

plugins.name: mycrew-pipeline
plugins.description: Layer 2/4 — the build pipeline. Six stages carry one task from a decision to shipped code: /how-to-do settles the fork, /do builds it, then /refactor, /review, /secure and /test harden it. In review and secure, the eyes that hunt are never the author's. Every stage weighs what actually changed and skips in one honest line when the change doesn't earn it.

plugins.name: mycrew-product
plugins.description: Layer 3/4 — the product plane and the board, both on backlog.md: everything true about the whole product above the sub-projects, and what is being done about it right now. /product-init founds the repo and stands the backlog up. /braindump and /ask-me draw the product out of you and file each piece — a milestone for a capability, a doc for what it concretely is; /propose-idea puts an idea in on your approval and logs every verdict as a decision. product-rules is the one rule set for what lands where; keep-the-board-honest plus board-chief/lead/worker keep the task board trustworthy — every card labelled by whose requirement it is, agent-born work drafted and gated before a worker is spent.

plugins.name: mycrew-crew
plugins.description: Layer 4/4 — the crew: the ones who actually build the product. Three characters, each handing down to the next. The chief is your deputy over the whole product, one to a product, owning the plane and delegating each approved feature whole. A lead holds one feature across every repo it touches, spawned as a background session of its own and reaching the other leads only where its feature depends on theirs. A worker carries one assignment end to end through the pipeline and hands back a four-field report. Each carries how it runs the rung below, so there is nothing to load and nothing to forget. Only the worker writes code.
